Download the `.dmg` from the latest release, open it, and drag **Ringkeeper** into **Applications**. 2. **Don't double-click it the first time:** the app isn't signed yet, so macOS won't open it that way. In Finder, choose **Go › Applications** from the menu bar, right-click **Ringkeeper** (or hold Control and click it), and choose **Open**. 3. macOS asks if you're sure. Click **Open**. It remembers this, so you only do it once. If that message has no **Open** button (macOS 15 or newer), click **Done**. Then open **System Settings › Privacy & Security**, scroll down to **Security**, and next to "Ringkeeper was blocked…" click **Open Anyway**. Confirm with your password or Touch ID, then click **Open**. If macOS instead says the app "is damaged and can't be opened", that's the same missing signature. In Terminal, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Ringkeeper.app`, then open it again. Your data goes in `~/Library/Application Support/Ringkeeper`, the master key in your Keychain, and new projects in `Documents/Ringkeeper`. Updates install from inside the app, as on Windows. Something not working on your Mac? Please open an issue: that's how the Mac build gets tested.

title: First run
text: 1. **Claude:** paste your Anthropic API key (or, for personal use, sign in with your Claude subscription). Ringkeeper checks it with Anthropic before saving. 2. **Projects:** add your first project, pick up the folders Claude Code already knows, or **Try it with demo data** to look around first. 3. **Connections:** connect a client's service, or skip for now. Then Home has a short **Get started** checklist and a three-step tour. See Concepts for how it fits together.

title: Moving to a new computer
text: Make a backup in Settings › Backup, install Ringkeeper on the new computer, and restore it there: see Backup. Running Ringkeeper on a server instead: Install with Docker.

title: Add-on tools (MCP servers)
text: Add-on tools give agents abilities Ringkeeper doesn't have built in: a web browser, a search engine, a service's own official tool. They're MCP servers; Ringkeeper runs them behind its gateway, keeps their keys, and checks each call.

title: Adding one
text: - **From the catalog** (Connectors › Browse connectors, or the first run): search, then sign in or paste a key. Some run on this computer (Ringkeeper installs them). - **From Claude Desktop:** Settings › From Claude Desktop imports the tools you already set up there; their keys move into Ringkeeper's vault. - **By address:** a tool that isn't listed, by its `https://` address. A tool that holds no client's data (a browser, your own files) can be a **shared tool**: yours, linkable to any client's projects.

title: What's held
text: Reading tools run. Everything else waits for your approval. Per tool, you can set it to need the connection's name typed, or to run without asking.

title: Undo
text: Ringkeeper can't undo what another tool's server does.

title: ElevenLabs
text: Voice agents, phone calls and speech, through ElevenLabs' own hosted server.

title: Sign in
text: Choose **ElevenLabs** and sign in with your ElevenLabs account. You approve what Ringkeeper may do on ElevenLabs' page, and there's no key to paste: ElevenLabs' server doesn't accept API keys. Connect one account per client, or your own. Sign-in works from the desktop app. A server install can't use this connection, because ElevenLabs only sends a sign-in back to the fixed address on this computer. Workspaces in ElevenLabs' EU, India and Singapore environments aren't on this tile yet.

title: What it can do
text: The tools are ElevenLabs' own, and **Connections** lists them once you've signed in. - **Reading runs.** Listing and reading agents, voices, conversations and the like. - **Anything else waits for your approval, every time:** creating or changing agents, placing calls, cloning voices, generating speech. "Trusted for an hour" doesn't apply here, and generating speech uses your ElevenLabs credits. - **Deleting needs the connection's name typed,** and can't be approved from Slack, Telegram or a notification. These rules go by a tool's name. You can make a tool stricter, never looser. Ringkeeper can't undo anything on ElevenLabs, and the card says so.

title: Where to get the key
text: A **personal access token** from Airtable: add the `data.records:read` and `schema.bases:read` scopes (and `data.records:write` if Ringkeeper may change records), and add **only this client's bases**. It starts with `pat`.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** list bases, tables (with their fields) and records; get one record. Each list says how many there are in all (records: counted up to 2,000), not only on the page it shows. - **Change:** create, update or delete up to 10 records at a time.

title: What's held
text: Reads always run. Changes run straight away on a staging or development connection, and wait for your approval on a production one. Changing or deleting records needs the connection's name typed to approve; adding records doesn't.

title: Narrowing it
text: On the client's page, a project's link can be limited to **one base** (its ID starts with `app`): calls from that project can't reach the client's other bases.

title: Undo
text: All three changes can be reverted for 7 days (Undo). Deleted records come back as new records, with new IDs.

title: Where to get the key
text: The **connection string**, starting with `postgresql://`: - **Supabase:** open the project, click **Connect**, and copy the **Session pooler** string. - **Neon:** open the project, click **Connect**, and copy the connection string. - **Any other Postgres** reachable from your computer: its usual connection string. Ringkeeper won't connect to an address on your own computer, or to itself. A database user that can only read is a good choice for a production database you only want reports from.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** list tables (with how many there are), describe a table, run a query. Every query runs inside a read-only transaction, one statement at a time. - **Change:** run one statement that writes (`INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, schema changes). A statement that only reads runs at once, even through this tool.

title: What's held
text: Reads always run. Changes run straight away on a staging or development connection, and wait for your approval on a production one. Deleting rows, dropping or altering tables, and anything the check can't read for certain need the connection's name typed to approve.

title: Undo
text: A plain `UPDATE` or `DELETE` on one table with a primary key can be reverted for 7 days (Undo). An `INSERT` and schema changes can't.

title: Long results
text: A query returns 200 rows unless the task asks for more, up to 1,000. When there are more, the answer says so, with the total and where to go on, and the task runs the same query from there. A statement that changed something is never run again to see more of its result.

title: Where to get the key
text: A fine-grained token (best): Resource owner = the client's organization (or you), **Only select repositories** (this client's), and Repository permissions **Contents, Issues, Pull requests, Metadata** (read and write to push and open issues and pull requests; read-only to only read). To have a routine watch its checks, add **Checks** (read-only). Everything else at No access. Set an expiry. A classic token (scope `repo`) only if the organization doesn't allow fine-grained ones. GitHub Enterprise Server: add its address.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** repositories, issues, pull requests, files, branches, commits, and the checks on a commit. Each list says how many there are in all, and for issues and pull requests of every state, how many are open. - **Change:** open and update issues, comment, open and merge pull requests, push a branch. A push never forces.

title: What's held
text: **Every change waits for your approval.** A merge needs the connection's name typed.

title: Narrowing it
text: Pin each project to the repositories it needs (`owner/name`; **Add another repository** for more than one): its tasks can't reach the token's other repositories. The gateway checks every call, a call that leaves the repository out gets it filled in when there's only one, and `list_repos` lists only the pinned ones. Your own GitHub connection (one token for several clients) linked to a client's project with no repository pinned says so: "This project could reach every repository this token can."

title: Undo
text: Changes on GitHub can't be undone by Ringkeeper.

title: Automation watch
text: A routine can start when a check fails or an issue is opened, to find out why and propose a fix. See Automation watch.

title: Gmail (app password)
text: The simple way to connect one mailbox. For Calendar, Drive and Sheets too, or for several accounts, use a Google account instead.

title: Where to get the key
text: An app password (Google needs 2-Step Verification on), and the Gmail address. A work admin may have turned app passwords off, and accounts with Advanced Protection can't use them.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** search mail and read messages (without marking them read). - **Change:** save a draft, send an email.

title: What's held
text: **Every email waits for your approval** before it's sent. Saving a draft doesn't wait: only you see it.

title: Undo
text: A sent email can't be unsent.

title: Long emails and attachments
text: A task reads the whole message, up to 200,000 characters at a time, as clean text: links keep their address and tables keep their rows. A longer one comes in parts, and each part says how long the message is and where the next part starts. The earlier messages a reply quotes are kept apart from what's new, and the task can ask for them. A task can also read a whole conversation, oldest message first, and an attachment: - **Its text:** PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint (with its speaker notes), CSV and text files, an attached email (.eml, or Outlook's .msg) and its own attachments, and a .zip, a file at a time. A long file starts with an outline: how many pages, which have text and which have pictures, and the first two pages. The task then reads the pages it needs, so one long PDF doesn't use up the task. - **A page as a picture:** the task can look at one page, or one picture, the way you see it. That keeps a table's or a chart's layout, which reading its text loses. - **A copy to work on:** saved in the project's `attachments` folder (where files you drop on a request go too), and listed with the task's files. Nothing changes in the mailbox. Looking at a page and saving a copy run without asking, and both are in Activity. Reading text from a picture or a scanned page needs the scan reader, a one-time download the desktop app offers the first time a task needs it. The pictures on a page that also has text are read too, like a price table pasted under a heading. A file it can't read, like a Numbers spreadsheet, is named, with what would work instead (a PDF or .xlsx copy).

title: Google (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Sheets, Docs, Search Console, Analytics)
text: Google accounts sign in through **your own Google app**: you make it once, for free, and then add as many clients' Google accounts as you need. This is in the desktop app.

title: Make the app (once, about 10 minutes)
text: **Settings › Developer apps** has every step with links that open the right page: 1. In the Google Cloud console, signed in with your own account, create a project. No billing needed. 2. Turn on the Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Sheets and Docs APIs. 3. **Google Auth Platform › Branding › Get started**: app name "Ringkeeper", audience **External**. Fill in the home page, privacy policy link and authorized domain that Settings shows, then save. 4. **Audience › Publish app.** Left in "Testing", Google signs accounts out after 7 days. 5. **Data Access**: paste the scopes Settings lists. 6. **Clients › Create client**: type **Desktop app**. Copy the client ID and secret (Google shows the secret only once) and paste both into Settings.

title: Add a Google account
text: **Settings › Developer apps › Add a Google account** (or the Google account tile under Connectors › Browse connectors), then sign in with the client's account. Google will say it hasn't verified the app: click **Advanced › Go to Ringkeeper**. It's your own app, so that's expected. Choose what it may do (mail, calendar, files, sheets) when you add it.

title: What waits for approval
text: Reading runs. Every write (sending, sharing, invites, edits, uploads, drafts, moving to the trash) asks you first. Per account, you can later let a tool run without asking, except sending: an email always asks, and more than 10 people at once needs the connection's name typed, in the app itself.

title: Good to know
text: - An unverified app can sign in up to 100 accounts over its whole life. - An account stops working if its password changes (for mail), if it's unused for six months, or if its owner removes Ringkeeper. Sign in again then. - A client's Workspace admin may need to trust your app's client ID.

title: Docs
text: Choose **Docs: read** or **Docs: read, create and edit** when you sign in, or later with Change access. An account added before Docs was here doesn't have it: open it under Connections, choose **Change access**, tick Docs and sign in again. If your Google app was made before then too, first turn on the Google Docs API and add the `documents` and `documents.readonly` scopes under Data Access. - **Reading a document runs:** its title and text, tables as rows. - **Making a document waits for your approval.** It's in the account's Drive, and only the account can see it until someone shares it. - **Editing a document waits for your approval, every time:** replacing a piece of text everywhere it appears, or adding text at the end. A document may be someone else's, so unlike other Google writes, you can't set an edit to run without asking. If the document changes between the request and your approval, the edit doesn't run; ask again. - Ringkeeper can't undo an edit. Google Docs keeps every version: **File › Version history**.

title: Search Console and Analytics
text: Choose **Search Console: read** and **Analytics: read** when you sign in, or later with Change access. Both only read: search clicks, impressions and positions, and Analytics reports. If your Google app was made before these were added, first turn on the Search Console, Analytics Data and Analytics Admin APIs, and add the `webmasters.readonly` and `analytics.readonly` scopes under Data Access.

title: YouTube
text: Choose what the account may do when you sign in, or later with Change access: **read videos and comments**, **upload videos**, **edit and delete videos, reply to comments**, and **read analytics**. First turn on the YouTube Data and YouTube Analytics APIs, and add the `youtube.readonly`, `youtube.upload`, `youtube.force-ssl` and `yt-analytics.readonly` scopes under Data Access. A sign-in reaches one channel: the one you pick on Google's page. **A video is private unless you choose otherwise.** Ringkeeper always sends its privacy, because YouTube's own default is public. - **Reading runs by itself.** - **A private video waits for your approval,** scheduled or not. A scheduled one goes public by itself at its time, and approving it is what allows that. - **Public and unlisted videos, edits, replies and deletes need the connection's name typed,** in the app itself. They can't be approved from a chat app. - **A time that has passed is refused,** even if it passed while the card waited: YouTube would publish at once. A video comes from the project's own folder. YouTube allows 100 uploads a day.

title: Long emails and attachments
text: A task reads the whole message, up to 200,000 characters at a time, as clean text: links keep their address and tables keep their rows. A longer one comes in parts, and each part says how long the message is and where the next part starts. The earlier messages a reply quotes are kept apart from what's new, and the task can ask for them. A task can also read a whole conversation, oldest message first, and an attachment: - **Its text:** PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint (with its speaker notes), CSV and text files, an attached email (.eml, or Outlook's .msg) and its own attachments, and a .zip, a file at a time. A long file starts with an outline: how many pages, which have text and which have pictures, and the first two pages. The task then reads the pages it needs, so one long PDF doesn't use up the task. - **A page as a picture:** the task can look at one page, or one picture, the way you see it. That keeps a table's or a chart's layout, which reading its text loses. - **A copy to work on:** saved in the project's `attachments` folder (where files you drop on a request go too), and listed with the task's files. Nothing changes in the mailbox. Looking at a page and saving a copy run without asking, and both are in Activity. Reading text from a picture or a scanned page needs the scan reader, a one-time download the desktop app offers the first time a task needs it. The pictures on a page that also has text are read too, like a price table pasted under a heading. A file it can't read, like a Numbers spreadsheet, is named, with what would work instead (a PDF or .xlsx copy). A file in Drive is read, looked at and saved the same way. A Doc, a Sheet or a Slides deck is looked at as its PDF, and saved as Word, Excel or PowerPoint.

title: Where to get the key
text: In n8n, open **Settings › n8n API** and create an API key (n8n's guide). Add your n8n's address too, like `https://n8n.acme.example`. n8n Cloud's free trial has no API.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** list workflows and their runs (executions), get one of each. A list of workflows says how many there are in all and how many are on, not only on the page it shows. - **Change:** turn a workflow on or off, replace a workflow, run a past execution again, stop a running one.

title: What's held
text: **Every change waits for your approval**, on any connection. Replacing a workflow needs the connection's name typed. A replaced workflow stays a draft unless the agent asks to put it live; approval is refused if someone edited the workflow after it was held.

title: One n8n for several clients
text: If your n8n holds several clients' workflows, make it your own tool and narrow each client project's link to a workflow tag or an n8n project. That project's tasks then see and change only those workflows and their runs. See A service you host for clients.

title: Undo
text: Replacing a workflow, and turning one on or off, can be reverted for 7 days (Undo). Re-running or stopping a run can't.

title: Automation watch
text: A routine can start when a workflow run fails, to find out why and propose a fix. See Automation watch.

title: Where to get the key
text: In the Twilio console: copy the **Account SID** from the home page, then **Account › API keys & tokens › Create API key** (Standard) and copy its SID and secret.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** phone numbers, messages, calls. - **Change:** send a text.

title: What's held
text: **Every text waits for your approval** before it's sent.

title: Undo
text: A text or a call can't be taken back.

title: Where to get the key
text: An **access token** from Vercel, scoped to this client's team (or one project), with an expiry date.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** teams, projects, deployments and their build logs, and the **names** of environment variables. Ringkeeper never reads their values. - **Change:** redeploy, put a deployment live (promote), roll back.

title: What's held
text: Reads always run. Changes run straight away on a staging or development connection, and wait for your approval on a production one.

title: Narrowing it
text: A project's link can be limited to **one team**, and optionally **one project**.

title: Undo
text: A deploy can't be undone by Ringkeeper. Put the earlier deployment live in Vercel (or ask Ringkeeper to promote it).

title: Automation watch
text: A routine can start when a deploy fails, to find out why and propose a fix. See Automation watch.

title: Developer apps
text: Some services only let an app you registered yourself sign in: Google, Microsoft (Entra), HubSpot, Salesforce, Xero, Intuit and Jobber. You register a free app with the service once, paste its client ID and secret into **Settings › Developer apps**, and then sign in as many accounts through it as you need. Each account is its own connection, a client's or your own, with the same rules as any other. The secret stays in the vault and never comes back to the page.

title: Set one up
text: Each service in **Settings › Developer apps** has its own steps, the address to paste, the scopes to add, and a link to the right page. When an app is saved, **Check it** asks the service whether it accepts the client ID and secret. Nothing is created by that check.

title: More than one app
text: A service can have several apps, for example one registered in a client's own tenant, when their admin only trusts that one. When a service has more than one, its sign-in asks which to use. Removing an app stops its accounts working at their next refresh.

title: Where the sign-in comes back
text: Most services want one exact address, and Ringkeeper's own port changes each launch, so they come back to a fixed address on this computer: `http://localhost:17845/oauth/callback`. It only answers on this computer. Nothing is opened to the internet. **Intuit, Xero, HubSpot and Salesforce** come back through a page instead: `https://yushkin.us/ringkeeper/oauth/callback`. These vendors want an https address, or won't take this computer's address for real accounts. It's a static page that passes the sign-in's code and state straight on to the address above, so Ringkeeper needs to be open on this computer. It keeps nothing, and a code can't be used without your app's secret, which stays in the vault. Ringkeeper checks the sign-in's state itself, as it does for every sign-in. On a server install, every service comes back to the server's own address.

title: Meta and Threads
text: Meta's apps come back through the https page, like HubSpot's. Your own Pages, Instagram accounts and Threads account work with no review from Meta, as long as you have a role on the app. A client's need Meta's review first: see Facebook Pages, Instagram and Threads. Change **Client accounts** on the app here once Meta has approved it. Google Ads uses your Google app, so it isn't a separate card. See Google Ads.

title: Good to know
text: - **Salesforce:** an app made in Setup works in the org it was made in. For a client's org, make one there and add it as another app. - **Microsoft:** a client's admin may have to allow your app in their tenant first. - **Xero:** apps made since March 2026 can only use the narrower scopes listed here. - **Intuit:** production keys need Intuit's app assessment first.

title: Where to get the password
text: Choose your provider and enter the address and password. Most providers want an **app password**, not your normal password: - **Gmail:** app passwords, which need 2-Step Verification. - **Zoho:** an app password if two-factor sign-in is on, with IMAP turned on in Mail settings. - **Yahoo:** Account security › Generate app password. - **Another provider:** its IMAP and SMTP servers too. **Microsoft:** for Microsoft 365, use the Microsoft account tile instead. Microsoft has turned password sign-in off for IMAP there, and is doing the same for SMTP.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** folders, searching, reading a message. Reading never marks mail as read. - **Change:** save a draft, move a message, send, move to the trash.

title: What's held
text: - **Reading runs.** - **Drafts, moving and sending** wait for your approval, even on test data. - **Deleting, and sending to more than 10 people at once,** need the connection's name typed, in the app. Chat apps and notifications can't approve those. - **A test to your own address runs by itself,** if you set one. The AI can't change where it goes.

title: Undo
text: Changes to a mailbox can't be undone here. A deleted message stays in the mailbox's trash for as long as your provider keeps it.

title: Long emails and attachments
text: A task reads the whole message, up to 200,000 characters at a time, as clean text: links keep their address and tables keep their rows. A longer one comes in parts, and each part says how long the message is and where the next part starts. The earlier messages a reply quotes are kept apart from what's new, and the task can ask for them. A task can also read a whole conversation, oldest message first, and an attachment: - **Its text:** PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint (with its speaker notes), CSV and text files, an attached email (.eml, or Outlook's .msg) and its own attachments, and a .zip, a file at a time. A long file starts with an outline: how many pages, which have text and which have pictures, and the first two pages. The task then reads the pages it needs, so one long PDF doesn't use up the task. - **A page as a picture:** the task can look at one page, or one picture, the way you see it. That keeps a table's or a chart's layout, which reading its text loses. - **A copy to work on:** saved in the project's `attachments` folder (where files you drop on a request go too), and listed with the task's files. Nothing changes in the mailbox. Looking at a page and saving a copy run without asking, and both are in Activity. Reading text from a picture or a scanned page needs the scan reader, a one-time download the desktop app offers the first time a task needs it. The pictures on a page that also has text are read too, like a price table pasted under a heading. A file it can't read, like a Numbers spreadsheet, is named, with what would work instead (a PDF or .xlsx copy).

title: Email sending (SMTP)
text: For sending through any provider: SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, Brevo, Amazon SES, your web host.

title: Where to get the key
text: From your email provider: the SMTP server, and a username and password or SMTP key. The connection is always encrypted, with SSL (usually port 465) or STARTTLS (usually port 587). The username defaults to the From address.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** which address it sends from. - **Change:** send an email, or a test to your own address.

title: What's held
text: - **Every email waits for your approval,** even on test data. - **More than 10 people at once** (To, Cc and Bcc together) needs the connection's name typed, in the app. Chat apps and notifications can't approve that. - **A test to your own address runs by itself,** if you set one. The AI can't change where it goes.

title: Undo
text: A sent email can't be unsent.

title: Where to get the key
text: In Resend, create an API key. It starts with `re_`. Sending access is enough to send; full access also lets the AI read domains and whether an email was delivered. The From address must be on a domain you verified in Resend.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** sending domains, and one sent email with its delivery status. - **Change:** send an email, or a test to your own address.

title: What's held
text: - **Every email waits for your approval,** even on test data. - **More than 10 people at once** needs the connection's name typed, in the app. - **A test to your own address runs by itself,** if you set one.

title: Undo
text: A sent email can't be unsent.

title: Any API
text: For a service with an HTTP API and no connection of its own. Give its address and how it signs in: a bearer token, a key in a header, a username and password, or a key in the address. If the API publishes an OpenAPI file, add its address too, and the AI can see what the API offers. **Forms On Fire** and **DataForSEO** have their own tiles, with the address filled in. The Forms On Fire tile is marked **Unverified**: its address and sign-in haven't been confirmed against Forms On Fire's own documentation, so check both in your account. Other regions and Appenate use their own.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** GET and HEAD anything under the address, and list its endpoints. - **Change:** POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE. A call can't leave the address: paths can't climb out of it, and redirects aren't followed, so the key is never carried somewhere else.

title: What's held
text: - **GET and HEAD run.** - **POST, PUT and PATCH** wait for your approval, even on test data: an API can do anything with a POST, and DataForSEO's cost money. - **DELETE** needs the connection's name typed, in the app. A project's link can be limited to a path, like `/v1/forms`.

title: Undo
text: Ringkeeper can't undo what an API call does.

title: File storage (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Vercel Blob)
text: Also any other S3-compatible service: MinIO, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces.

title: Where to get the key
text: Make a key limited to this client's bucket. - **AWS S3:** an access key and its secret, and the region. - **Cloudflare R2:** an R2 API token's access key and secret, and your account ID from the R2 overview page. - **Vercel Blob:** open the Blob store and copy its read-write token. It starts with `vercel_blob_rw_`. A Blob store has no buckets. - **Another service:** its address, region, access key and secret.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** list buckets, list files, read a file: text as it is, and the text in PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and .zip files (a long one starts with its outline, then page by page). Anything else, up to 2 MB, comes as it is. - **Look and keep:** look at a PDF's page or a picture the way you see it, and save a copy in the project's `attachments` folder to work on. - **Change:** upload a file, delete a file.

title: What's held
text: - **Listing, reading, looking and saving a copy run.** Looking and saving are in Activity. - **An upload** waits for your approval, even on test data. - **Deleting** needs the connection's name typed, in the app. A project's link can be pinned to a bucket and a folder, so each project stays on its own files.

title: Undo
text: Uploads and deletes can't be undone here. Versioning in the bucket, if you turn it on, keeps earlier copies.

title: Clerk
text: Read and manage an app's users, sessions and organizations through Clerk's Backend API. One connection is one instance of one app. Each instance has its own secret key, so a client's development and production instances are two connections, marked as test data and production. The key says which it is: `sk_test_` for development and `sk_live_` for production. Ringkeeper won't let a live key be labelled as test data.

title: Add it
text: In the Clerk Dashboard, pick the application and the instance, open **API keys**, and copy the secret key. Then use the **Clerk** tile under Connectors. If `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` is in a project's `.env` file, Ringkeeper offers it on the project's page. The key reaches that one instance and nothing else, so linking the connection to a project is what scopes it.

title: What's held
text: - **Runs:** reading users, sessions, organizations, invitations and the instance's settings. - **Waits for approval:** updating metadata, and sending or taking back invitations. - **Needs the name typed, in the app:** deleting, banning or locking users, ending sessions, changing organization roles or members, deleting organizations, and anything that changes sign-in settings, including allowlists and blocklists. Metadata that sets a role, plan or permission also needs the name typed, because an app often uses it to decide what someone may do. So does an organization invitation with any role other than `org:member`. Metadata edits can be undone for 7 days. Nothing else here can be undone from Ringkeeper.

title: Good to know
text: - Ringkeeper uses Clerk's Backend API, not its hosted MCP server: that server signs in as a Dashboard user and has no tools for metadata, invitations, bans, sessions or organizations. - A few things are left out on purpose: setting a password, signing in as a user, and anything that answers with a secret.

title: How it signs in
text: Add your Microsoft app in **Settings › Developer apps**, then sign in from the tile with the account, and choose what it may do. Each account is its own connection.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** mail and attachments, calendars and events, OneDrive and SharePoint files (what's in them too) and who can reach them. A task can also look at a page of a file as a picture, and save a copy in the project to work on. - **Change:** send and draft email, mark and move messages, add and change events, answer invitations, add, rename, move and copy files and folders. It can't upload a file, set a mail rule or auto-reply, or reach another person's mailbox.

title: What's held
text: - **Every write waits for your approval,** even on test data. - **More than 10 recipients or attendees** needs the connection's name typed, in the app. - **So do** sending a saved draft and replying to all, because how many people it reaches can't be seen from the call. - **So does** deleting mail, events or files, canceling a meeting, and sharing a file or making a link to it.

title: Undo
text: An edit to a draft, an event, a message's marks, or a file's name can be undone. A sent email can't be unsent.

title: Long emails and attachments
text: A task reads the whole message, up to 200,000 characters at a time, as clean text: links keep their address and tables keep their rows. A longer one comes in parts, and each part says how long the message is and where the next part starts. The earlier messages a reply quotes are kept apart from what's new, and the task can ask for them. A task can also read a whole conversation, oldest message first, and an attachment: - **Its text:** PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint (with its speaker notes), CSV and text files, an attached email (.eml, or Outlook's .msg) and its own attachments, and a .zip, a file at a time. A long file starts with an outline: how many pages, which have text and which have pictures, and the first two pages. The task then reads the pages it needs, so one long PDF doesn't use up the task. - **A page as a picture:** the task can look at one page, or one picture, the way you see it. That keeps a table's or a chart's layout, which reading its text loses. - **A copy to work on:** saved in the project's `attachments` folder (where files you drop on a request go too), and listed with the task's files. Nothing changes in the mailbox. Looking at a page and saving a copy run without asking, and both are in Activity. Reading text from a picture or a scanned page needs the scan reader, a one-time download the desktop app offers the first time a task needs it. The pictures on a page that also has text are read too, like a price table pasted under a heading. A file it can't read, like a Numbers spreadsheet, is named, with what would work instead (a PDF or .xlsx copy). A OneDrive or SharePoint file is read, looked at and saved the same way.

title: Where to get the key
text: HubSpot has no pasted key here. Add your own HubSpot app in Developer apps, then sign in from the tile. Your app's scopes decide what can be reached.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** the account, contacts, companies, deals, tasks, owners, pipelines, properties and sequences. - **Change:** add or edit contacts, companies, deals and tasks, and add notes. - **Reach people:** send a marketing email, or enroll a contact in a sequence.

title: What's held
text: - **Adding and editing wait for your approval,** even on test data. - **Deletes, merges and bulk edits** need the connection's name typed, in the app. - **Sending email and sequence enrollment** need the name typed.

title: Undo
text: HubSpot edits can't be undone here.

title: Where to get the key
text: Salesforce has no pasted key here. Make an External Client App in your org, add it in Developer apps, then sign in from the tile. The connection remembers your org's address, like `acme.my.salesforce.com`, and sends its token nowhere else.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** SOQL queries, SOSL searches, org limits, object fields, and single contacts, accounts, opportunities, leads and tasks. A query reaches whatever the signed-in user can see. - **Change:** add or edit contacts, accounts, opportunities, leads and tasks, and add notes. - **Reach people:** send an email. Nothing here can run Apex or a batch of arbitrary requests.

title: What's held
text: - **Adding and editing wait for your approval,** even on test data. - **Deletes and sending email** need the connection's name typed, in the app.

title: Undo
text: An edit to a contact, account, opportunity, lead or task can be undone. It puts back the standard fields, and a field that was empty before stays as the edit left it. Custom fields aren't put back.

title: Where to get the key
text: In Pipedrive, click your account name, then Company settings, Personal preferences and API, and copy your token. It acts as you, with your permissions.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** people, organizations, deals, activities, notes, pipelines and stages. - **Change:** add or edit people, organizations, deals and activities, and add notes. An edit can't delete a record, change who can see it, or change someone's marketing status.

title: What's held
text: - **Adding and editing wait for your approval,** even on test data. - **Deletes and merges** need the connection's name typed, in the app.

title: Undo
text: An edit to a person, organization, deal or activity can be undone. It puts back the main fields, and a field that was empty before stays as the edit left it. Custom fields aren't put back.

title: Where to get the key
text: In Keap, open Settings, then API Settings, add a key and name it. The token shows once, so copy it then. A Personal Access Token acts as you. A Service Account Key has admin access, and only an admin can make one.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** the business profile, contacts, companies, opportunities and stages, tasks, tags, campaigns and users. - **Change:** add or edit contacts, companies, opportunities and tasks, and add notes. - **Reach people:** send an email, tag contacts, or add them to a campaign sequence.

title: What's held
text: - **Adding and editing wait for your approval,** even on test data. - **Deletes and merges** need the connection's name typed, in the app. - **Sending email and adding to a sequence** need the name typed. - **Tagging needs the name typed too,** because a tag can start an automation.

title: Undo
text: An edit to a contact, company, opportunity or task can be undone. For a contact it puts back the name only. A field that was empty before stays as the edit left it.

title: Jobber
text: This one shows as Unverified. Jobber shows its current API schema only to signed-in developers, so the operations were checked against the schema in its app template and its changelog.

title: Where to get the key
text: Jobber has no pasted key here. Make an app in the Developer Center, add it in Developer apps, then sign in from the tile. The scopes you tick there decide what can be reached.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** clients, jobs, quotes, invoices, work requests, visits and users. - **Change:** add or edit clients, jobs and quotes, and add notes to clients and jobs. - **Reach people:** email a quote or invoice to a client.

title: What's held
text: - **Adding and editing wait for your approval,** even on test data. - **Archiving a client, and deleting jobs or quotes,** need the connection's name typed, in the app. - **Emailing a quote or invoice** needs the name typed.

title: Undo
text: Jobber edits can't be undone here.

title: Where to get the key
text: Sign in to Housecall Pro as an admin, open My Apps, then All Apps, and find API Key Management. Generate a key, name it, and choose full or read-only access. The API needs the MAX plan or above. Housecall Pro's guide has more.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** the company, customers and their addresses, employees, jobs, line items, appointments, estimates, leads and invoices. - **Change:** add or edit customers, add jobs, job notes and line items, move appointments, add leads, and turn a lead into an estimate or job.

title: What's held
text: - **Adding and editing wait for your approval,** even on test data. - **Changing a job's time needs the name typed,** unless the call sets both `notify` and `notify_pro` to false, so nobody is told. - **An estimate with a schedule needs the name typed,** unless `notify_customer` is false. - **Dispatching a job, approving an estimate, bulk line item edits and deleting an appointment** need the connection's name typed, in the app.

title: Undo
text: An edit to a customer can be undone, and a field that was empty before stays as the edit left it. Nothing else can be undone here.

title: ServiceTitan
text: You can't connect ServiceTitan yet. Its calls need a token traded for a client ID and secret, and Ringkeeper can't do that trade yet. The rules below are ready for when it can.

title: Where to get the key
text: In the ServiceTitan Developer Portal, register an app and connect it to your account. You'll need its Client ID, client secret and application key, and your tenant ID.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** business units, technicians, customers, locations, leads, jobs, appointments, estimates, invoices and payments. - **Change:** add or edit customers, leads and jobs, edit locations, add notes, move appointments, and add estimates. An edit can't deactivate a customer or change their credit and payment terms. Invoices and payments are read-only.

title: What's held
text: - **Adding and editing wait for your approval,** even on test data. - **Cancelling a job, deleting an appointment and marking an estimate sold** need the connection's name typed, in the app.

title: Undo
text: An edit to a customer, location, lead or job can be undone. It puts back the main fields, and a field that was empty before stays as the edit left it. An address isn't put back.

title: How it signs in
text: Add your Intuit app in **Settings › Developer apps**, then sign in from the tile and choose the company. Each company is its own connection. A sandbox company counts as test data.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** profit and loss, balance sheet, cash flow, trial balance, aged receivables and payables, and any record through a search. - **Change:** customers, vendors, estimates and purchase orders. - **Money:** invoices, bills, payments, bill payments, expenses and journal entries.

title: What's held
text: - **No write ever runs by itself,** even on a sandbox. - **Estimates, purchase orders, customers and vendors** wait for your approval. They don't touch the books. - **The name typed, in the app:** invoices and bills, because QuickBooks has no drafts and creating one posts it. So do payments, expenses, journal entries, sending, voiding and deleting.

title: Undo
text: Nothing here can be undone by Ringkeeper. Void or delete the record in QuickBooks instead.

title: How it signs in
text: Add your Xero app in **Settings › Developer apps**, then sign in from the tile and choose the organisations. One sign-in can reach several, so a call names one, and a project's link can be narrowed to one.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** profit and loss, balance sheet, trial balance, aged receivables and payables, bank summary, invoices, bills, contacts, payments, quotes, purchase orders and journals. - **Change:** contacts, and draft invoices, bills, credit notes, quotes and purchase orders. - **Money:** approve, void and email invoices, record payments, bank entries, transfers and manual journals.

title: What's held
text: - **No write ever runs by itself,** even on a demo company. - **A new record with no status, or status DRAFT,** waits for your approval. So do contacts. - **The name typed, in the app:** any other status, approving, editing an invoice, sending, voiding, deleting, payments, bank entries, journals, and a contact's bank details. An edit needs the name because the call can't show the invoice is still a draft.

title: Undo
text: Nothing here can be undone by Ringkeeper. Void or delete the record in Xero instead.

title: Where to get the key
text: In Wave's developer portal, open Manage Applications, create an application, and make a full access token for it. The token reaches every business in your Wave account, so each call names a business.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** businesses, customers, vendors, products, sales taxes, invoices, estimates, payments, and the chart of accounts with balances. - **Change:** customers, products, estimates and invoices. - **Money:** approve and send invoices, record payments and transactions. Wave's API has no reports and no bills. Account balances are the closest it offers.

title: What's held
text: - **No write ever runs by itself,** even on test data. - **Draft invoices, estimates, customers and products** wait for your approval. - **The name typed, in the app:** approving, sending, payments, money transactions, editing an invoice, deleting, and any invoice that doesn't say it's a draft. An edit needs the name because the call can't show the invoice is still a draft. Wave's approval can't be taken back.

title: Undo
text: Nothing here can be undone by Ringkeeper. Delete a draft in Wave instead.

title: How it signs in
text: Add your Microsoft app in **Settings › Developer apps**, with the Business Central API permission, then sign in from the tile and give the environment's name, like Production or Sandbox. One connection is one environment, and a call names the company.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** trial balance, balance sheet, income statement, cash flow, aged receivables and payables, customers, vendors, accounts, ledger entries, invoices, payments and journals. - **Change:** draft sales and purchase invoices and their lines. - **Money:** post, send and cancel invoices, add customer payments and journal lines, post a journal.

title: What's held
text: - **No write ever runs by itself,** even in a sandbox. - **Draft invoices** wait for your approval. A draft isn't on the books. - **The name typed, in the app:** posting, sending, canceling, deleting, payments and journal lines.

title: Undo
text: An edit to a draft invoice's dates and details can be undone. Nothing else can: a posted invoice is canceled in Business Central, with a credit memo.

title: Where to get the key
text: Sign up for a BILL developer account, in the sandbox or in production, and generate a developer key. You'll need four things: the username, password, organization ID (it starts with `008`) and developer key. Then type the address: `gateway.prod.bill.com` for real data, or `gateway.stage.bill.com` for the sandbox. Add one connection per organization and environment. Ringkeeper signs in with these and gets a short session, so use a BILL user made for this, with only the access it needs. **To pay bills,** BILL also needs its MFA ID and device name. They come from BILL's MFA sign-in, which sends a code to your phone, and they last 30 days. Ringkeeper doesn't run that step, so a connection without them can read and draft but can't pay.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** bills, vendor payments, payment options, vendors, vendor credits, invoices, payments received and customers. - **Change:** bills, invoices, customers and vendors, and make an invoice's payment link. - **Move money:** pay a bill, cancel or void a payment, charge a customer's saved bank account, and send an invoice.

title: What's held
text: - **Reading runs by itself.** - **Bills, invoices, payment links, customers and vendors wait for your approval,** every time. Nothing here can be trusted for an hour. - **Paying a bill, charging a customer, cancelling or voiding a payment and recording a payment** need the connection's name typed, in the app. So does **sending an invoice** and **archiving** anything. - The approval card shows the amount, the vendor or customer and the account in large text. A cancel or void names the payment, because BILL's call doesn't state an amount. Bank accounts are left out, for vendors, customers and your own organization, and so are users, bulk payments and bill approvals.

title: Undo
text: A customer or vendor edit can be undone. A payment or a sent invoice can't.

title: Where to get the key
text: In the Shopify admin, open **Apps**, then **Develop apps**, pick the store's custom app, and copy its Admin API access token. Give the app only the access it needs. Then type the store address, like `acme.myshopify.com`. One token reaches one store, so add one connection per store. Only custom apps made before January 2026 have a token to paste. Newer apps are made in Shopify's Dev Dashboard and use short-lived tokens, which this connection can't get yet.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** the store, products, orders, customers, draft orders, collections, pages, blog articles, themes and sales channels. - **Change:** draft products, customers, order notes, draft orders, and draft pages and articles. - **Go live:** publish or activate, change prices in bulk, refund, cancel or fulfil an order, and change themes and store policies.

title: What's held
text: - **Reading runs by itself,** orders and customers too. - **A product created as a draft waits for your approval.** So does a customer, a draft order, or a page or article created as unpublished. - **Publishing, activating, or changing a status** needs the connection's name typed, in the app. A new product only counts as a draft if the call says `DRAFT`. - **Bulk price changes, refunds, cancelling or fulfilling an order, deleting, themes and store policies** need the name typed too. - An edit to something already live, with no change of status, only waits for approval. Check the card before you approve it.

title: Undo
text: Nothing here can be undone yet. A refund or a cancelled order can't be taken back.

title: Where to get the key
text: In Ghost Admin, open **Settings**, find **Integrations**, and add a custom integration. Copy its Admin API key, which looks like `id:secret`. Then type the domain you open Ghost Admin on, like `acme.ghost.io`. One key reaches one site.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** the site, posts, pages, tags, newsletters, tiers, offers and members. - **Change:** draft posts and pages, tags and members. - **Go live:** publish, schedule or unpublish, send a newsletter, delete, and change the active theme.

title: What's held
text: - **Reading runs by itself.** - **A post or page created as a draft waits for your approval,** and so do tags and members. Only a call that says `draft` counts as a draft. - **Publishing, scheduling, unpublishing and sending a newsletter** need the connection's name typed, in the app. So does **deleting** and **changing the theme**. - An edit to a live post, with no change of status, only waits for approval. Check the card before you approve it. Ghost's settings are left out, because reading them can answer with keys and writing them can change keys. So are staff users, integrations and webhooks.

title: Undo
text: Nothing here can be undone yet. A sent newsletter can't be unsent.

title: Where to get the key
text: In the Square Developer Console, open your application and choose **Credentials**. Pick Production or Sandbox at the top and copy the access token. Then type that environment's address: `connect.squareup.com` for real data, or `connect.squareupsandbox.com` for the sandbox. Each has its own token, so add one connection per environment.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** the account and its locations, payments, refunds, payouts, customers, orders, invoices, payment links, the catalog, subscriptions and disputes. - **Change:** customers, orders, draft invoices and payment links. - **Move money:** charge a saved source, capture or void a payment, refund, send an invoice, change a subscription, and answer a dispute.

title: What's held
text: - **Reading runs by itself.** - **Customers, orders, draft invoices and new payment links wait for your approval.** - **Charges, captures, voids, refunds and subscription changes** need the connection's name typed, in the app. So does **sending an invoice**, because it can charge a saved card. - **Accepting a dispute or adding evidence** needs the name typed too, and so does anything that deletes. - The approval card shows the amount, currency, customer and account in large text. A capture or void names the payment, because Square's call doesn't state an amount. Card and bank account numbers never pass through Ringkeeper: a charge uses a token from Square's own payment form.

title: Undo
text: A customer edit can be undone. A charge, refund or sent invoice can't.

title: Where to get the key
text: In Helcim, open **All Tools**, then **Integrations**, then **API Access Configurations**. Choose **New API Access**, set its Access Restrictions, and create it. The restrictions narrow what the token can do: refunds need the Admin level of transaction processing. A developer test account has its own token, so add one connection per account.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** card and ACH transactions, card batches, customers and their saved cards (as tokens), invoices, recurring plans and subscribers. - **Change:** customers and invoices. - **Move money:** charge or hold a saved card, capture, refund, void, take an ACH payment, and manage subscribers.

title: What's held
text: - **Reading runs by itself.** - **Customers and invoices wait for your approval.** - **Charges, captures, refunds, voids, ACH payments and subscription changes** need the connection's name typed, in the app. - The approval card shows the amount, currency, customer and account in large text. A charge uses a saved card token. Helcim's payment call can also take a full card number: Ringkeeper refuses any call that carries one.

title: Undo
text: A customer edit can be undone. A charge or refund can't.

title: Where to get the key
text: In Lemon Squeezy, open **Settings**, then **API**, and create a key. A key made in test mode reaches test data only, and keys last a year. The Test button says which mode a key is in.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** stores, customers, products, variants, orders, subscriptions and their invoices, discounts and checkouts. - **Change:** customers, checkout links and discount codes. - **Move money:** refund an order or a subscription invoice, and change or cancel a subscription.

title: What's held
text: - **Reading runs by itself.** - **Customers, discounts and checkout links wait for your approval.** - **Refunds and subscription changes** need the connection's name typed, in the app, and so does deleting a discount. - The approval card shows the amount and the order in large text. A refund with no amount is a full refund, and the card says the amount isn't stated. License keys and files are left out, because they answer with the key or a download link. A customer or subscription record carries a signed link to that customer's billing page, valid for a day. The AI sees it when it reads the record.

title: Undo
text: Nothing here can be undone. A refund can't be taken back.

title: Where to get the key
text: In the Clover Merchant Dashboard, open **Settings**, **View all settings**, then **Ecommerce API Tokens**. Create a token for an API integration and copy the private token. It belongs to one merchant. Then type the address: `scl.clover.com` for real data, or `scl-sandbox.dev.clover.com` for the sandbox. Clover's Ecommerce API serves the US and Canada.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** charges, refunds and online orders. - **Change:** orders, and customers saved with a card token. - **Move money:** refund a charge or return an order. New charges aren't available here yet. Clover needs the customer's own internet address on each one, and Ringkeeper can't send it yet. Recurring plans aren't here either: they live at a different Clover address.

title: What's held
text: - **Reading runs by itself.** - **Orders and customers wait for your approval.** - **Refunds and returns** need the connection's name typed, in the app, and so does removing a saved card. - The approval card shows the amount and the charge in large text.

title: Undo
text: Nothing here can be undone. A refund can't be taken back.

title: Where to get the key
text: In the Braintree Control Panel, open your API settings and copy a public and private key. Then type the address: `payments.braintree-api.com` for real data, or `payments.sandbox.braintree-api.com` for the sandbox. Sandbox and production have different keys, so add one connection per environment.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** transactions, refunds, customers and disputes. - **Change:** customers. - **Move money:** charge or hold a saved payment method, capture, refund, void, and answer a dispute.

title: What's held
text: - **Reading runs by itself.** - **Customers wait for your approval.** - **Charges, captures, refunds, voids and dispute answers** need the connection's name typed, in the app, and so does deleting a customer or a saved payment method. - The approval card shows the amount, customer and account in large text. Braintree charges in the merchant account's currency, which the call doesn't state. Anything that takes card details or hands out a client token is left out: a charge uses a payment method already saved in Braintree.

title: Undo
text: Nothing here can be undone. A charge or refund can't be taken back.

title: Plaid
text: Not available yet: the table is written, and it needs a change in Ringkeeper first.

title: Where to get the key
text: In the Plaid Dashboard, open **Developers**, then **Keys**, and copy the client ID and the secret for your environment. Then paste the access token your own Plaid integration holds for one linked bank. Ringkeeper doesn't link banks, so one connection is one bank you've already linked.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** the bank's accounts, live balances, transactions, recurring payments, the account owners on file, investment holdings and transactions, and which statements exist.

title: What's held
text: Nothing is held, because nothing can change. Every operation only reads. There's no way to move money here: transfers and payments are left out entirely. Full account and routing numbers are left out too, so account details stop at the last few digits.

title: Undo
text: Nothing changes, so there's nothing to undo.

title: Oracle Database
text: Your own Oracle Database, or an Autonomous Database with its wallet. Nothing else needs installing: Ringkeeper connects in thin mode, with no Oracle client.

title: Add it
text: Use the **Oracle Database** tile under Connectors, with a user that has only the access it needs. The connect string looks like `db.example.com:1521/orclpdb1`. For an **Autonomous Database**, download the wallet `.zip` from its Database connection page, choose it in the form, and use one of its service names as the connect string, like `acme_high`. Ringkeeper uses only `ewallet.pem` and `tnsnames.ora` from it. The wallet is kept in the vault and unpacked only for the length of a call. If a project's `.env` has `ORACLE_DSN`, `ORACLE_USER` and `ORACLE_PASSWORD`, Ringkeeper offers it on the project's page.

title: What's held
text: The same checks as a Postgres database: - **Reading runs,** in a read-only transaction. - **On production,** every change waits for your approval. On test data, changes run and are logged. - **Needs the name typed:** deleting rows, dropping or changing tables, permissions, and anything that can't be checked, including PL/SQL blocks and calls to your own functions. A plain `UPDATE` or `DELETE` on one table with a primary key can be undone for 7 days.

title: Good to know
text: - An Oracle function can write even inside a read-only transaction, so a query that calls a function Ringkeeper doesn't know has to go through `execute`, where it's checked. - Oracle's `q'[...]'` strings can hide what a statement does, so they count as something that can't be checked. - Values use `:1`, `:2` binds.

title: Clouds: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and OCI
text: Each runs the cloud's own server on this computer, with the login you already have in its command line tool. Ringkeeper holds no cloud key: it only tells the server which profile to use. This is in the desktop app.

title: Add one
text: Sign in with the cloud's command line tool (`aws sso login`, `az login`, `gcloud auth login`, or your OCI config). **Connectors** then lists the login under **Signed in on this computer**. Connect it, and it's your own tool. The first run downloads the server, so it needs `uv` for AWS and OCI, and Node.js for Azure and Google Cloud. The form says if one is missing.

title: Keeping clients apart
text: One Azure, Google Cloud or OCI login can often reach many clients, so **each project's link has to name the client's own** subscription, project or compartment. Until it does, the project's calls are refused. A command that names a different one is refused too. For AWS, one connection is one profile, so one account. A link can also pin a region. On OCI, a command on a project's link has to name that compartment, because Ringkeeper can't tell which compartment a resource ID belongs to. Listing commands get it added. Flags that would leave the login, like `--profile`, `--account` or `--endpoint-url`, are always refused.

title: What's held
text: What a command needs comes from the command, not the tool: - **Runs:** list, describe, get. - **Waits for approval:** update, modify, tag, stop, copying files. - **Needs the name typed, in the app:** deleting, creating or starting anything that costs money, anything on IAM, and whatever hands out a secret. So does any command Ringkeeper doesn't recognize. Azure's tools go by their names, the same way. A per-tool setting can make these stricter, never looser. Nothing here can be undone from Ringkeeper.

title: Good to know
text: - These use your login's own permissions, so give it no more than you want used. - Oracle marks its server as not meant for production use. - Versions are pinned, and change only with a Ringkeeper update.

title: Where to get the key
text: In Bluesky, open **Settings**, then **Privacy and security**, then App passwords, and add one. Paste it here with your handle, like `yourname.bsky.social`. Don't use your account password: Ringkeeper refuses anything that doesn't look like an app password. Add one connection per account. It's free, and there's no review.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** profiles, an account's posts with their likes, reposts and replies, a post's thread, notifications, and search. - **Post:** a post or a reply, with a link card if you want one. Links in the text become real links by themselves. - **Delete:** a post. Pictures and video aren't available yet, and neither are direct messages.

title: What's held
text: - **Reading runs by itself.** - **Posting, replying and deleting need the connection's name typed,** in the app itself. They can't be approved from a chat app, and nothing here can be trusted for an hour. - **Bluesky has no drafts.** A post waits on its approval card until you answer it.

title: Undo
text: A post can't be undone here. Delete it instead.

title: Facebook Pages, Instagram and Threads
text: All three sign in through an app of your own at Meta. See Developer apps for how to add one. **Your own accounts work now, with no review from Meta.** You need a role on the app, and the connection goes in as a shared tool, so it isn't tied to one client. Then pick the Page or account each project may use. **A client's account needs Meta's review first.** That means Tech Provider status, App Review and Business Verification. Until then the client's tile says **Needs Meta review** and won't sign in. Once Meta approves your app, change **Client accounts** on the app in **Settings > Developer apps**. Sign-in hasn't been completed against a real Meta app yet, so these tiles say Unverified.

title: Where to get the key
text: Add the app in **Settings > Developer apps**, then sign in from the tile: - **Facebook Pages:** pick the Pages it may reach on Meta's page. - **Instagram:** the account must be a professional one, linked to one of those Pages. - **Threads:** add the Threads use case to your app. It has its own app ID and secret. If Meta says **Invalid Scopes**, a permission is missing from your app. Meta adds only a few by itself. Open the app's **Dashboard**, select the use case, click **Customize**, and click **Add** next to each one the message names.

title: What it can do
text: | | Facebook Pages | Instagram | Threads | |---|---|---|---| | Read | Posts, scheduled posts, comments, insights | Posts, comments, insights, posts left today | Posts, replies, insights, posts left today | | Prepare | Scheduled or unpublished posts | A post, kept unseen for a day | A post or reply, kept unseen | | Publish | Posts, comments and replies | Posts and replies | Posts and replies | | Hide | Comments | Comments | Replies | | Delete | Posts and comments | Posts and comments | Posts | Instagram and Threads fetch pictures and video from a public address. Instagram pictures must be JPEG. Neither can schedule through this API, so Facebook Pages are the only ones here that do. Direct messages aren't available yet.

title: What's held
text: - **Reading runs by itself.** - **Anything nobody can see yet waits for your approval:** a scheduled or unpublished Page post, or a prepared Instagram or Threads post. Hiding a comment waits too. - **A scheduled Page post goes out by itself at its time.** Approving it is what allows that. - **Publishing, editing a post, replying and deleting need the connection's name typed,** in the app itself. They can't be approved from a chat app, and nothing here can be trusted for an hour.

title: Good to know
text: - Each Page keeps its own token. A project held to one Page can't see or reach another. - A Threads sign-in lasts 60 days, and Ringkeeper renews it while it's in use. Left unused for that long, sign in again. - Meta's docs want an app's secret on a server. Here it's in your computer's vault, like every other app's.

title: Undo
text: None of these can be undone here. Delete a post instead, or edit it.

title: Google Ads
text: Google Ads signs in through your Google app, so there's no new app to add and no developer token: Google retired those on 2026-09-09. Access now belongs to the Google Cloud project that owns your app.

title: Where to get the key
text: 1. In that project, turn on the Google Ads API. 2. On the API's overview page, open **Upgrade access level** and apply for **Explorer**. Google usually approves it by itself. Stay on Explorer or Basic: Standard adds an audit. 3. Sign in from the Google Ads tile, with a Google account that can reach the ad account. 4. On each project's link, set the **Ad account** it may use: the 10-digit customer ID. An application can be turned down if the project is on Google Cloud's Free Trial, or its billing is suspended. Google suggests upgrading or removing billing, and removing it costs nothing. A client under a manager account needs the manager's ID too, and tasks can pass it.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** any report in Google Ads Query Language, and the accounts this sign-in reaches. - **Pause:** a campaign, an ad group or an ad. - **Create:** a Search campaign with its daily budget, ad groups, responsive search ads and keywords. Everything starts paused. - **Spend:** start a campaign, an ad group or an ad, and change a daily budget or a bid. Only Search campaigns can be made here for now. Payment methods and billing aren't reachable at all, and neither are creating accounts or changing who has access.

title: What's held
text: - **Reports run by themselves.** - **Pausing waits for your approval.** It only stops spending. - **Creating, starting, and changing a budget or a bid need the connection's name typed,** in the app itself. They can't be approved from a chat app, and nothing here can be trusted for an hour. - **The card shows the spend and what it's for,** like `50.00 USD a day` on **Budget: Spring promo**, with Google's ID beside it. Ringkeeper asks Google for those names when the call is held, which is one of the day's operations. If Google doesn't answer, the card shows the IDs. Just before the change runs, Ringkeeper checks that currency against the account. Starting a campaign also checks its real budget. If either differs from the card, nothing changes. - **Approving a new campaign declares it has no EU political advertising.** Google won't make a campaign without that answer, so the card says it in full. If it isn't true, deny the card. A campaign that has any can't be made here.

title: The daily operations
text: Google gives each Cloud project one daily allowance, and every client's calls share it: | Level | Operations a day | |---|---| | Explorer | 2,880 | | Basic | 15,000 | | Standard | No limit | **Settings > Developer apps** shows what's been used in the last 24 hours, under Google. Set the level there to match what Google gave you. A report is one operation, each change is one, and more pages of a report are free. Google still counts calls it refuses. This is what this install sent, so Google's own count can differ.

title: Undo
text: Nothing here can be undone by Ringkeeper. Pause it, or change it back with a new approval.

title: Notion and agent memory
text: Agents can keep notes between runs: decisions, preferences, how a client's things are set up. Each project has its own notes. Choose where they live for every project at once, in **Settings › Memory › Notion for every project**, or for one project in its **Settings**, under **Memory**: - **Ringkeeper (local)** is the default. Notes stay on this computer. - **Notion** keeps them in a Notion database you can read and edit yourself. Each project's **About** says where its notes go, with a link to its Notion database. An agent can also have its own choice, in its settings. It can keep notes locally while the project uses Notion, or the other way round.

title: Where to get the key
text: Notion memory uses its own connection, **Notion memory**, not the Notion connection in the catalog. That one reaches whatever your account can see. This one reaches only the pages you share with it, so Notion itself keeps agents' notes where you put them. 1. In Notion, open your connections and create an internal connection. A workspace owner has to do this. Copy its token. 2. Add **Notion memory** under Connections and paste the token. Add it as a shared tool to use it for every project, or for one client. 3. In Notion, open the page the notes go under, choose **••• > Connections**, and add it. 4. Choose where notes go: - **For every project:** in **Settings › Memory › Notion for every project** (or on the connection's card), pick the connection and one root page, and choose **Use Notion for every project**. It needs a shared connection. - **For one project:** in the project's **Settings**, open **Memory**, choose **Notion**, pick the connection and the page, and save. For one project, Ringkeeper makes a database under that page called `<Client> › <Project> › Ringkeeper memory`, with one row per note: the note, the agent, the date and the task it came from. You can pick a database that's already there instead. For every project, it makes a page per client under the root page (`<Client> › Ringkeeper`) and each project's database under its client's page, so one client's page never holds another client's notes. A project already in Notion keeps its place. A new project gets its database when its first task starts; if Notion doesn't answer then, its notes stay here that time, and it's tried again on the next task. **Stop for new projects** keeps every project where it is now. A Notion memory connection only holds notes: it isn't linked to projects, and no task calls it as a tool. Its **Test** button still checks the token. Links made before 0.1.0-beta.38 were removed.

title: What agents keep
text: Every task starts with its project's latest notes (and Shared notes and My memory, if they're on), so it doesn't have to search for what an earlier task found. Before it finishes, it saves what a later run would otherwise have to find again: where things live (IDs, bases, tables, workflows, files and pages it found by listing or searching, even obvious ones), decisions and corrections you gave, how this client wants things done, and gotchas that cost it steps. Not the task's result, one-off facts or secrets: one to three short notes, or none. A task's answer mentions memory only when it saved something. Its page and the conversation show **Saved to memory** under the result, with each note. Check my setup only reads, so it keeps nothing. You can add notes yourself, with the same rules and in the same place: - **Add a note** on the project's **Memory** (in its Settings). - **Remember this** under a result or a reply: edit the text, and save it. - Say **"remember that …"** in a conversation. When it's clear which project (the one chosen at the top, the one the message names, or the one the conversation is about), it's saved straight away, with no task, and the reply says what was saved and where. Otherwise the request is routed as usual.

title: What it can do
text: - **Agents** have two tools, `recall` and `remember`. Neither takes a place: a run reaches its own project's notes and nothing else, and it can't delete a note. Your other Notion connection keeps its own holds. - **You can add a row** in Notion, or have Claude or Claude Code add one. It's picked up on the next run. Text written inside a row's page counts too. - **Edits in Notion win.** Change a note there, and that's what agents read. - **Delete a row and it's forgotten.** Deleting a note in Ringkeeper moves it to Notion's trash. If Notion doesn't answer, nothing is forgotten. Agents read the last copy and are told it may be out of date.

title: What's held
text: - **Reading and adding notes run by themselves,** and each one is in Activity. - **No secrets.** A note with a token, a password, or a card or bank number is refused, and the same things are hidden from agents if someone types them in Notion. A project's notes may keep a business contact's email address. - **Notes are treated as information, not instructions.** Agents are told so, and a note can't change what needs your approval.

title: Good to know
text: - A client's memory page can't be attached to another client's project, and the page above it can't be shared between clients either. - A client's Notion connection only works for that client's projects. - A note is at most 2,000 characters.

title: Shared notes
text: **Settings > Memory > Shared notes** is one Notion page of your own knowledge across clients. It needs a shared connection. Every project can read it, unless you turn it off in that project's Memory, and agents can't write there unless you allow it. Keep client data out of it.

title: My memory
text: **My memory** is for what's yours, across every client: your preferences, your style, how you work. It's a Notion database of your own, so it works on any Notion plan. 1. Add **Notion memory** as a shared tool, and share a page with it in Notion. 2. Open **Settings > Memory > My memory**, pick the connection and the page, and save. Ringkeeper makes a database called `My memory` under that page. Agents search it when they start, and add lasting preferences when they finish. You can add and edit rows there too. A project can leave it out, in its own **Memory** settings.

title: What your own memory can't hold
text: This covers My memory, Shared notes and Notion AI memory: - **Nothing about a client.** A save naming a client, a project's full display name, or the address of a client's connection is refused. Names match as whole phrases, and one common word on its own, like website, app, crm or portal, never counts. - **Nobody's details.** Email addresses, phone numbers and street addresses are taken out, and the rest is kept. - **No secrets.** A token, a password, or a card or bank number is refused. The check goes by names, so a client's fact that doesn't name them can't be caught. Agents are told to keep those in the project's own memory.

title: Notion AI memory
text: **Needs Notion Business plan or higher,** with Notion AI. It's off until you turn it on. It uses Notion's own personal memory instead of a database of yours. On other plans, use My memory. 1. Add **Notion** from the catalog as a shared tool, and sign in with your own account. A token won't do: memory needs a signed-in person. 2. Open **Settings > Memory > Notion AI memory** and turn it on. Memories must be on for you and your workspace: in Notion, **Settings > Notion AI > Memory > Use memories**. If Notion doesn't offer the tools, Ringkeeper says so. Press **Refresh its tools** after changing that. - **Searching, reading and saving run by themselves.** Saves and refusals are in Activity. - **Deleting a memory needs the connection's name typed.** Editing one waits for your approval. - **A save about someone else is refused,** and so is any memory call on a client's connection.

title: Undo
text: Rows deleted from Ringkeeper can be restored from Notion's trash. Local notes can't be undone.

title: Leadfeeder
text: Leadfeeder (by Dealfront) shows which companies visit a website. It connects through Leadfeeder's own MCP server. You can add it for a client, or as your own shared tool. **It needs a paid Leadfeeder plan.** On the free plan only sign-in and the account list work: everything else comes back refused. The connection's card says so, and tasks that hit it stop there instead of trying again. After upgrading, press **Test**.

title: Where to get the key
text: There's no key to paste: Leadfeeder's server takes a sign-in only. The API key in your Personal settings is for Leadfeeder's other API, so Ringkeeper leaves one in a project's `.env` file alone. 1. Add **Leadfeeder** under Connections and sign in. Your account needs API and MCP access, and your user needs the **Manage API keys and use API** permission. In a company workspace, an admin may have to approve the connection. 2. Press **Test**. It lists the Leadfeeder accounts this sign-in reaches, with their IDs. 3. On each project's link, set the **Leadfeeder account** it may use. Each account tracks one website. A project can't use Leadfeeder until that's set.

title: What it can do
text: - **Read:** website visits, companies, contacts, lists, tags, custom fields, and how many credits a job would cost. - **Change:** tags, lists, custom fields, feeds and goals. - **Spend credits:** open a company's or contact's full details, find contact data, and enrich companies.

title: What's held
text: - **Reading runs by itself.** - **Changes wait for your approval.** That covers tagging, adding to lists, and making lists, tags and custom fields. - **Anything that may spend credits waits, and the card shows the cost.** Jobs show Leadfeeder's own estimate, like `About 120 credits`. Opening records shows the most it can cost, like `Up to 3 credits`: a record you opened in the last 12 months is free. If Leadfeeder can't estimate a job, the card says `Credits not known`. - **Deletes need the connection's name typed,** in the app itself.
