So do the cookie consent and data processing settings. - **Nothing here can be trusted for an hour,** and none of it can be approved from a chat app when it needs the name typed. Leadfeeder asks for its own confirmation on these calls. Your approval in Ringkeeper answers it, so you only approve once, and an agent can't confirm anything itself.

title: Undo
text: Nothing here can be undone by Ringkeeper. Credits spent stay spent.

title: Cal.com
text: Bookings, event types, schedules and availability, through Cal.com's own hosted server.

title: Sign in
text: Under **Connections**, choose **Cal.com** and sign in with your Cal.com account. You approve what Ringkeeper may do on Cal.com's page, and there's no key to paste: Cal.com's hosted server signs in rather than taking an API key. Connect one Cal.com account per client, or your own. Sign-in works from the desktop app and from a server install. A `CAL_API_KEY` in a project's `.env` is noticed when you add the project, and left there: Cal.com connects from its tile. If you connected before Cal.com added contacts, teams or organizations to what its server can do, disconnect and sign in again to grant them.

title: One team or the whole account
text: A project's link to the connection reaches the whole account unless you narrow it. To keep a project to one team, set **Cal.com team** to the team's ID number when you link it. Then: - a call that names another team is refused; - a call that leaves the team out gets it filled in; - a tool that works across the whole account, like your own bookings or your list of teams, isn't available on that link. Cal.com's help, your profile and links into its app still are. Cal.com also checks your role in the team on every call.

title: What it can do
text: The tools are Cal.com's own, and **Connections** lists them once you've signed in. - **Reading runs.** Bookings, event types, schedules, availability, busy times, contacts, teams and Cal.com's help. - **Bookings wait for your approval, every time:** creating, rescheduling, cancelling or confirming one, marking an absence, adding an attendee. Each of these can email real people, so "Trusted for an hour" doesn't apply here. - **Every other change waits too:** creating or changing event types, schedules, routing forms, memberships, invites and your profile. - **Deleting needs the connection's name typed:** an event type, a schedule, a membership or a contact. It can't be approved from Slack, Telegram or a notification. - **Its tool for any API operation** goes by the operation's name: a `get` or `list` runs, a delete needs the name typed, and anything else waits. These rules go by a tool's name. You can make a tool stricter, never looser. Ringkeeper can't undo anything on Cal.com, and the card says so.

title: PageSpeed Insights
text: Google's free check of a page's speed: the Lighthouse scores, Core Web Vitals from real visitors when Google has them, and the fixes that would save the most time.

title: Where to get the key
text: PageSpeed Insights needs a Google Cloud API key. It's free. 1. In the Google Cloud console, pick a project or make one. Your Google app's project works. No billing needed. 2. Turn on the PageSpeed Insights API. 3. Under **APIs & Services › Credentials**, choose **Create credentials › API key**. Restrict it to the PageSpeed Insights API. 4. Under **Connectors › Browse connectors**, choose **PageSpeed Insights** and paste the key. One key works for every client's sites, so add it as **your own tool** and link it to the projects that need it. **Test** checks the key on example.com. A `PAGESPEED_API_KEY` in a project's `.env` is found when you add the project.

title: What it can do
text: - **Check a page:** its address, on a phone (the default) or a computer, for performance and, if asked, accessibility, best practices and SEO. A check takes 10 to 60 seconds. - The answer is the part people act on: the scores out of 100, the lab metrics (Largest Contentful Paint, Total Blocking Time, Cumulative Layout Shift and more), real visitors' numbers when Google has enough of them, and up to five fixes with the time each would save.

title: What's held
text: Nothing: it only reads. A check loads the page the way a visitor's browser would, and changes nothing. The key goes to Google in a header, never in an address.

title: Recipes that use it
text: - **Weekly speed check:** every Monday, checks the site's main pages and compares with last week. - **Monthly search and speed report:** puts Search Console's clicks next to each page's speed, with your Google account.
